questions.q: In Windows File Explorer, which shortcut creates a new folder in the current location?
questions.solution: Ctrl+Shift+N creates a new folder in Explorer. Plain Ctrl+N opens a new Explorer window. In Chrome, Ctrl+Shift+N opens an incognito window.
questions.shortcut: Ctrl+N = new window; add Shift for a new folder.

questions.q: The Windows feature that automatically detects and configures a newly connected USB printer is:
questions.solution: Plug and Play lets the OS identify new hardware, install its driver and configure it without manual setup. Hot swapping is only the connect/disconnect-while-running part; overclocking raises clock speed; mirroring is disk redundancy.
questions.shortcut: 'Automatically detects AND configures' = Plug and Play.

questions.q: A hub operates at which OSI layer?
questions.solution: A hub only repeats electrical signals — **Layer 1**, no addressing at all.

questions.q: The Intel 4004, released in 1971, is historically important because it was the first:
questions.solution: Intel 4004 (1971) was the world's first commercially available microprocessor - an entire CPU on one chip - and it launched the 4th generation of computers.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

The proteins in millets are higher than **most cereals**.
questions.solution: Proteins must be compared with proteins → **those of most cereals** (plural). 'That of' is singular; the original compares proteins with cereals — unlike things.
questions.shortcut: name both sides of the comparison before choosing.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

The boys said, "Let us play football."
options: The boys told that they played football.
The boys asked if they played football.
The boys suggested to play football.
questions.solution: 'Let us' = suggestion → **suggested + V-ing** (or suggested that they should play). B breaks the gerund pattern; C misreads it as a statement; D misreads it as a question.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The paediatrician ___ the mother to complete the full course of medicine.
questions.solution: The sentence needs a finite past verb after its subject: **advised**. *Advice* is a noun, *advices* is not standard English, *advising* cannot serve alone as the verb.
questions.shortcut: Frame first: subject + blank + object → finite verb → advised.

questions.q: Select the correct passive form of the sentence: 'They had already locked the gate before we reached.'
options: The gate has already been locked before we reached.
The gate was already being locked before we reached.
The gate had already being locked before we reached.
The gate had already been locked before we reached.
questions.solution: Past perfect row → **had already been locked**; the before-clause stays as it is. 'Has already been locked' upgrades the tense and clashes with the past clause; 'was already being locked' rewrites the row as past continuous; 'already being' puts being in a perfect slot.
questions.shortcut: had + V3 → had been + V3, adverbs stay put.

questions.q:
Consider the statements:
1. The first Cricket World Cup was played in 1975.
2. India won the ODI World Cup in 1983 and 2011.
3. The Santosh Trophy is a tennis event.
Which are correct?
questions.solution: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — the **Santosh Trophy is football** (inter-state championship).

questions.q: Tropical cyclones in the north-west Pacific Ocean (near China, Japan and the Philippines) are called:
questions.solution: They are **typhoons**. The same kind of storm is a **hurricane** in the Atlantic/Caribbean and a **cyclone** in the Indian Ocean. A tornado is a small land funnel, not a tropical cyclone.

questions.q: Who is known as the **'Grand Old Man of India'**?
questions.solution: **Naoroji** — thrice Congress president, first Indian MP in the British House of Commons (1892), author of the drain theory.

questions.q: The **Treaty of Salbai (1782)** concluded —
questions.solution: **Salbai (1782)**, signed under Warren Hastings, ended the **First** Anglo-Maratha War (with Nana Fadnavis' Pune regime).

questions.q: The value of $(\cosec\theta - \sin\theta)(\sec\theta - \cos\theta)(\tan\theta + \cot\theta)$ is:
questions.solution:
$\cosec\theta - \sin\theta = \frac{\cos^2\theta}{\sin\theta}$; $\sec\theta - \cos\theta = \frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos\theta}$; $\tan\theta + \cot\theta = \frac{1}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}$.

Product $= \frac{\cos^2 \cdot \sin^2}{\sin\theta \cdot \cos\theta \cdot \sin\theta\cos\theta} = 1$.
questions.shortcut: Convert all three, cancel to $1$. Trap: $0$ (assuming one bracket vanishes — none does).

questions.q: After allowing a discount of 10% on the marked price, a trader gains 8%. The marked price is what per cent above the cost price?
questions.shortcut: 18% is 8 + 10 — percentages of different bases do not add.

questions.q: The average monthly salary of 20 employees is ₹18,000. When the manager's salary is added, the average rises by ₹1,500. The manager's monthly salary is:
questions.shortcut: $19500 + 20 \times 1500 = ₹49{,}500$. (₹48,000 uses the OLD average as his own share.)

questions.q: After two equal successive discounts, an article marked at ₹6,400 is sold for ₹5,184. Each discount is:
questions.solution: Kept fraction $= \frac{5184}{6400} = 0.81 = 0.9^2$ → each discount $= 10\%$.
questions.shortcut: 9.5% halves the total 19% — successive discounts do not split evenly.

questions.q: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 144 144" width="144" height="144" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><line x1="12" y1="132" x2="132" y2="132"/><line x1="72" y1="12" x2="132" y2="132"/><line x1="12" y1="132" x2="72" y2="12"/><line x1="42" y1="132" x2="72" y2="12"/><line x1="72" y1="12" x2="102" y2="132"/><line x1="12" y1="132" x2="102" y2="72"/><text x="72" y="7.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">A</text><text x="5" y="139.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">B</text><text x="42" y="145.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">C</text><text x="102" y="145.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">D</text><text x="139" y="139.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">E</text><text x="110" y="75.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">F</text><text x="40" y="109.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">G</text><text x="89.1" y="75.1" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">H</text></svg>
questions.solution: Without line BF, the two lines from A give (3 × 4)/2 = 6 triangles on the base BE. Line BF crosses AC at G and AD at H and creates more. Full list (corners named as in the figure): ABC, ABD, ABE, ABF, ABG, ABH, ACD, ACE, ADE, AFG, AFH, AGH, BCG, BDH, BEF. Total = **15**.
questions.shortcut: Start from the apex-line value 6, then add every triangle that uses line BF.

questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 34 34" width="34" height="34" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><line x1="5" y1="5" x2="17" y2="17"/><line x1="5" y1="17" x2="17" y2="17"/><line x1="17" y1="5" x2="17" y2="17"/><line x1="17" y1="5" x2="29" y2="17"/></svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 46 46" width="46" height="46" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><line x1="5" y1="17" x2="17" y2="5"/><line x1="5" y1="41" x2="17" y2="29"/><line x1="17" y1="17" x2="29" y2="29"/><line x1="17" y1="29" x2="29" y2="29"/><line x1="29" y1="17" x2="29" y2="29"/><line x1="29" y1="17" x2="41" y2="29"/><line x1="29" y1="41" x2="41" y2="29"/></svg>
questions.solution: The part is made of 1 horizontal stroke, 1 vertical stroke and 2 slanting strokes. All of its strokes appear together, in the same directions, only in the correct option, in its **middle-right**. Each wrong option is one stroke away from the part: a stroke missing, re-angled or replaced - so the part does not actually appear there.

questions.q:
Select the pair of numbers that can replace the two question marks (?) in the following series, in order.

**2, 5, 10, ?, 26, ?, 50**
questions.shortcut: Each visible term is one more than a square.

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 60 60" width="60" height="60" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><polygon points="6,6 54,6 54,54 6,54"/><circle cx="15" cy="15" r="2.6" fill="currentColor"/><circle cx="15" cy="21" r="2.6" fill="currentColor"/><circle cx="33" cy="45" r="2.6" fill="currentColor"/></svg>
questions.solution: A punch goes through every layer, so it opens into one hole per layer. Unfold in reverse order, mirroring the holes across each fold line: the count goes 2 - 3.
questions.shortcut: Count first: each full fold doubles the holes; then check positions.
